newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 6.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Government proposes a new electoral system which combines territorial and proportional representation, but will do away with preferential voting. Proposal made by Justice Minister G.L. Peiris to parliamentary select committee debating constitutional changes.
Central Bank's Automated Clearing House not affected by Thursday's one-day token strike by some employees, a bank statement says.
Parliament votes to pass emergency regulations that govern the country by one more month.
Air force planes destroy Tamil rebel camp at Kantalaimadu northwest of Welioya on Wednesday, killing at least 25 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels.

Rotary International presents President Chandrika Kumaratunga with special award for personally getting involved in Sri Lanka's attempts to eradicate polio. Among previous recepients of this award are Britian's former prime minister John Major and Indonesian President Suharto.

Trade unions complain that the Colombo port, South Asia's transshipment hub, has about 4,000 employees who have been hired mostly due to their political connections, a fact which erodes the port's performance and profitability.
Southwest monsoon, which usually arrives by first week of June, delayed by about one week, Meteorological Department says.
A Sri Lankan aborigine shoots friend after mistaking him for a bear in the island's remote northeastern jungles. Both were out hunting, police said.
